Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. Lko.

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant; Shri Ashutosh Mishra, learned counsel for the complainant, learned AGA and perused the record.

2. The FIR in question was lodged alleging that the daughter of the informant was being victimized for dowry and on not being able to pay the dowry, the daughter of the informant was killed and the same was shown as suicide.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant argues that in the inquest report, it was recorded that the body was recovered and lowered by the police authorities.
He further argues that in the inquest report it is shown that the hands were tied behind the back.
He further argues that even as per the information of the Panch, the cause of death was suicide.
He further argues that a suicide note was recovered which clearly demonstrates that there was no demand of dowry.

The deceased has stated in the Akhilesh Pratap Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93595511/
1 suicide note that she was committing suicide because her mother-in-law as well as sister-in-law (Jethani) wants to perform the Terahi function of her (the deceased's) mother.

entities.text: Akhilesh Pratap Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She also stated and expressed that the children of the deceased should be taken care of by her mother.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant further draws my attention to the post-mortem report which shows the cause of death as ante-mortem hanging.
He further draws my attention to the medical report of the panel of doctors which have explained that the cause of death is hanging.
As regards the minor injuries recorded on the wrist, the panel was of the view that the same was on account of the bangles.
The panel was of the view that the cause of death was ante-mortem hanging.
He argues that the mother-in-law and the sister-in-law have already been enlarged on bail by this Court vide separate orders passed on 04.07.2023.
He argues that in the suicide note, which is a vital piece of evidence, there is no allegation of any demand of dowry.
Section 304B IPC cannot be said to be made out.
The applicant has no criminal antecedent and should be enlarged on bail.

5. Learned counsel for the informant and learned AGA strongly oppose the bail application by arguing that the allegations with regard to demand of dowry are mentioned in the FIR as well as in the statement of one of the sisters of the deceased and also in the statement of the informant given subsequent to the FIR.
He further argues that apart from the ligature mark, other injuries are also visible on the wrist.
He further argues that from the inquest report, it is clear that hands were found tied behind the back, which cannot be done by a person who commits suicide.
6. Learned counsel for the complainant argues that the applicant is a very influential person and with huge difficulty, the FIR could be lodged with the intervention of the senior police officers.
He argues that the suicide note does not demonstrate that the same was written immediately before the incident.
7. In the light of the arguments raised at the Bar, it is clear from the records that the cause of death is ante-mortem hanging.
The suicide note does not indicate any demand of dowry.
The injuries other than the ligature mark are minor and have been explained by the panel of doctors and prima-facie, are not related to the incident in question.
The applicant has no criminal antecedent, as such, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Akhilesh Pratap Singh be released on bail in FIR No.14 of 2023, under Section 498A, 304B, 323, 504, 506 IPC & Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Baba Bajar, District Ayodhyabad/Faizabad on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him Akhilesh Pratap Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93595511/
2 from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
